newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's 3-yr yields end at fresh 1997 high.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's 3-yr yields end at fresh 1997 high.

text.p: Yields on three-year benchmark corporate bonds closed at a new year high of 12.53 on Friday on lingering fears of a liquidity squeeze, dealers said.
They said major investors were low-key in general due to the twice-a-month deadline to meet the central bank's won reserve requirement.
* Overnight average call rates at 12.08 against 12.30
Out of 150 billion won worth of new issues on Friday, about 229 billion won worth failed to find buyers, dealers said.
"Since the Hanbo loan scandal, investors seemed to shy away from companies with poor guarantors or gloomy earnings prospects," said a Daewoo Securities dealer.
Major investors kept a low profile on Friday to meet the twice-a-month deadline of won reserve requirement with the central bank.
"The corporate yield is expected to test 12.60 next week and hover around that level for the time being," said a LG Securities dealer. -- Yeom Yoon-jeong (822) 727 5647
